# Size of the amendment 4 coverage design on (s3c-ann-net)'s own forecasts, HAC beside (#1516)

**Hypothesis and step:** H5, step M5 (registration). **Development data, not a verdict.** Generated by `scripts/coverage_size_1516.py page` from `docs/research/coverage-size-1516/result.json`, not edited by hand. It answers her ruling of 8 November 2026 on the coverage failure of PR #1513 ("measure"): registration of #1510 waits on it, and the rule registration applies is hers.

**What was measured.** The design amendment 4 sets (Kupiec and Christoffersen independence at q05/q95 and q01/q99, leads 1 to 5, each regime, every h-th decision day at lead h, Holm over the family at 5.0%) was run on 2000 null draws per world. A null draw is a forecaster calibrated by construction, in every (lead, regime) cell of the candidate's 1855 development decision days (targets to 2025-12-31). In the `bootstrap` worlds it keeps the candidate's own serial and cross-lead structure: its randomised PITs are ranked to an exact uniform margin within each lead and regime (so its own miscalibration is removed) and whole decision days are resampled by a stationary bootstrap within each regime, the same days at all five leads. In the `iid` control the PITs are independent uniforms. Beside the iid Kupiec, the HAC family replaces it by a Kupiec with a Bartlett (Newey-West) variance at lag h - 1 on every day (`method="hac"` of `coverage_cells`); the independence test is the same in both. Seed 1516. The strict hit rule is the only rule here: no outcome equals the candidate's quantile at a read level (ties by level: q0.01 0, q0.05 0, q0.95 0, q0.99 0), so the three rules of #1513 coincide.

The engine's p-values equal `scoring_protocol.coverage_cells`' on the candidate itself under both methods, and the two verdicts equal `enforce_coverage_requirement(..., family="holm", alpha=0.05, rule="strict")` (flag patched on inside one call; it is False in the tree). The walk reproduces the 1314 record's mean grid CRPS to 1e-9.

## Family-wise size: how often the design rejects a calibrated forecaster

Share of null draws with at least one Holm rejection across the family of 200 cells (nominal 5.0%), with a Wilson 95% interval. In the `bootstrap` worlds the independence test is not at its size: the world keeps the candidate's dependence, so its rejections there are power against that dependence. The `iid` row is the design's size.

## The candidate under each reading

| Reading | passes | tests | rejected by Holm (5%) | smallest raw p | Monte Carlo p of that smallest p, `bootstrap_10` | `iid` control |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| iid Kupiec (amendment 4 as set) | **FAIL** | 200 | 11 | <0.001 | 0.023 | <0.001 |
| HAC Kupiec | **FAIL** | 200 | 10 | <0.001 | 0.919 | 0.832 |

The Monte Carlo p is the share of null draws whose smallest raw p-value in the family is at most the candidate's own: how often a calibrated forecaster with the candidate's dependence (or none) looks at least as bad as the candidate on the family's most extreme test.

## What this shows and does not show

- It shows how often this design, as `coverage_cells` and `enforce_coverage_requirement` apply it, rejects a forecaster that is calibrated by construction in every cell, when that forecaster has the candidate's own dependence from day to day and across leads, and with none; and how the candidate reads under an iid or a HAC Kupiec. It is development evidence on seen days and no verdict.
- The world is a resample of the candidate's own PIT ranks. It keeps dependence in blocks of the stated mean length (5, 10 and 20 days), not any longer-range structure, and it assumes the candidate's dependence is the same under the null as in the data; where the dependence is the candidate's miscalibration (volatility clustering the forecast fails to follow), a world that keeps it is a world in which the independence test has power, not size.
- The hit rule is the strict one: with no ties at the four read levels the deterministic and the randomised tie rules coincide here, and the size of the randomised rule on a whole-basis-point world is #1156's, not repeated.
- Why the HAC family over-rejects a calibrated forecaster in the `iid` control: the Bartlett variance is centred at the nominal hit rate, not at the sample rate, so a cell with no hit at q01 or q99 gets a variance of about p squared and a Kupiec p-value far below any Holm threshold (pinned in `tests/test_coverage_size_1516.py`, `HacZeroHitTests`). With cells this thin, one zero-hit cell fails the family.
- A HAC variance changes the Kupiec test only; the independence test and the thinning are the same in both families. It is not tuned: lag h - 1, as `coverage_cells` sets it.
- The 2026 days (near-blind tier), B1, B1', B2 and B4, and the uncapped secondary version are not read. Nothing here changes amendment 4, `COVERAGE_REQUIREMENT_IN_FORCE` or any threshold.
